items.q: What's the fix for um, uh, and so?
items.a: Replace every filler with **silence** — a pause. Fillers signal scatterbrain; **pauses signal confidence and clarity**. *"Every time you feel the urge to say um, uh — just pause."*

items.q: How do you stop trailing off into vocal fry?
items.a: Give **every word the same breath/energy as the first**. Trailing sentence ends make you sound unfinished and unprofessional.

items.q: Why do "sorry / I think / I might be wrong" hurt at work?
items.a: These **apology prefixes / softeners** make ideas **walk in limping** — listeners get permission to dismiss you before the idea lands. Prefer **direct statements**.

items.q: Should you speed up when you're nervous?
items.a: No — **slow down**. Rushing is like **Chopin at 2×**: right content, wrong experience. Pauses calm you and the room and give your brain time to think.

items.q: How do you stop making the talk about your anxiety?
items.a: Shift to **audience-consciousness**: *"It's not about you — it's about the people you're about to serve"* (Vinh's CEO backstage fix for **2,500** people). Serve them, don't consume bandwidth on self-obsession.

items.q: What's wrong with speaking your thoughts out loud?
items.a: Unstructured thinking dumps **loose parts on the doorstep**. Structure first with frameworks like **PARA**: Point → Action → Result → Ask — so the listener assembles nothing in real time.

items.q: How do you stop answering with endless backstory?
items.a: Fight **backstory overload**: **repeat their question**, answer in **one short sentence**, then offer more only if asked. Anxiety makes you front-load context they didn't request.

items.q: What do you do instead of interrupting?
items.a: Wait until they finish, hold **2 seconds of silence**, then ask *"Tell me more about that."* Interrupting is usually **discomfort with silence**, not urgency.

items.q: How do you cure main-character syndrome in conversation?
items.a: Use the **three-for-one ratio**: **three questions about them** for every **one story about you**. Dale Carnegie via Vinh: the most interesting people are the most **interested in everyone else**.

items.q: Why is "sounding the same your whole life" the #1 habit?
items.a: One vocal register reads as **one personality**. Your voice is an **88-key instrument** — most people play **five familiar keys**. Adapting register to context (camera vs lunch vs kids) is authenticity, not fakeness.
